hybrid, and the cap is the product decision rather than a limitation to hide. the phrasebook always
writes the reading, so the page is complete before any request happens. the first 100 readings of a
day can additionally ask groq for three fresh lines. past that the page says so plainly instead of
degrading into errors.

the arithmetic behind the cap: the payload measures 326 bytes, about 120 tokens, plus a ~350 token
system prompt and ~80 tokens out, so roughly 550 per call. groq free tier gives 100k tokens a day,
which is ~180 calls. capped at 100, comfortably inside, plus 3 per ip so one visitor cannot drain it.

what leaves the device, asserted by test not by copy (train/bulut_check.mjs):
  {gun, mesaj, konusma, cevap_hizli_dk, cevap_yavas_dk, gecikme_orani, baslatma_pay, gece_pay,
   en_uzun_sessizlik_gun, kirilma_sayisi, kirilma_var, degisenler, birlesik_olasilik}
  no message text, no names, no raw timestamps, 326 bytes. names were dropped on purpose so
  'only numbers leave' is literally true rather than nearly true.

the model may not write digits. the worker rejects any line containing one and the client checks
again, so every figure on screen comes from the engine. this is the failure the live spiker had
when it quoted lines that were never in the chat, and here it cannot happen by construction.

backend/worker.js gains /api/zaman and /api/zaman-kalan. reading the counter does not spend one, so
the offer shows a true number before the user decides. NOT DEPLOYED: the key is Damla's, needs
`cd backend && npx wrangler deploy`. until then the client gets no answer and stays silent.
